Three directions, same real data

Same three items (Kinder, Pistachio, Margherita), same real prices and photos from Supabase, same card component, same cart trigger. Only the token layer changes between columns. Screenshots, not swatches, captured at 390px and 1024px.

Logo finding: pulled the real mark from the old host and sampled it pixel by pixel. The chimney-cake icon and the "Valhalla" script are pure black ink (~54 unique colors, the black cluster is all anti-aliasing of one ink color). The pink is only this export's background canvas fill, #ea87b7, and it doesn't even match the #BE185D the old site declared in its own theme-color meta tag. Rose was a UI choice by the previous developer, not something in the mark. Free to move it.

A. Refined Rose

Kept as brand, everything else rebuilt around it. The safe continuity option: the color already associated with this cafe (even if only through old UI, not the mark) stays, and the argument for it is recognition, not origin.

1024px

390px

B. Fire-Lit Hall

Ember, charcoal, brass. Valhalla is a firelit mead-hall in the old stories, this is the first pass that actually looks like that instead of borrowing a color that happened to be on a hosting template.

1024px

390px

C. Toasted Amber

My own option. Not the myth, the food: the color of caramelized sugar on a chimney cake actually cooked over an open flame. Distinct hue from both A and B, and it's the one thing every single product on the menu literally has in common.

1024px

390px

All three use the same neutral-warmth logic (dark, layered, no flat single color), the same type, the same radius rule, the same card component. Only accent hue, base warmth, and background glow differ. Pick one and the rebuild (background, card, cart-as-sheet, item detail with deep links, tablet breakpoints) proceeds against it.
